subject: beaver
title: Beavers Chew Trees All Day, and Iron Keeps Their Teeth Sharp

scenes.text: Beavers chew trees all day and their teeth never wear out. The secret is in the color.
Look closely. Those front teeth are orange-brown, not white like yours.
That color is iron, packed into a thin layer of enamel just a few hundredths of a millimeter thick.
Scientists tested it. Iron enamel is harder than normal enamel, and it resists acid better, even fluoride-treated enamel.
Yours has magnesium instead. A beaver's teeth are built from the same blueprint, with different chemistry.
So the beaver's orange smile isn't stained. It's armor.

description:
Beavers chew trees all day and their teeth never wear out.
Their orange front teeth contain iron in the enamel, which makes it harder and more acid-resistant than normal enamel.
Would you trade your teeth for these?
